cluster_stories.title: US official says Nvidia has begun shipping powerful H200 AI chips to China
cluster_stories.summary: In May, ⁠Reuters reported ⁠the Commerce Department had cleared around 10 Chinese firms to buy the H200, but no deliveries had been made at the time. Sources said at the time that Alibaba, Tencent and ​ByteDance were among those approved.
cluster_stories.headline: NVIDIA SHIPS H200 AI CHIPS TO CHINA... Export Approvals Clear

cluster_stories.title: US National Science Foundation to ban projects with flagged Chinese institutions
cluster_stories.summary: The United States’ National Science Foundation (NSF) is set to ban collaborations with Chinese research institutions designated as restricted entities, as well as their employees, under a new policy that moves away from seeking to balance security risks with the benefits of international collaboration. The policy reflects a broader congressional push by House Republicans to curb academic partnerships between China and the US, amid lawmakers’ concerns that such ties could contribute to Beijing’s...
cluster_stories.headline: US BANS NSF PROJECTS WITH FLAGGED CHINESE AI INSTITUTIONS

cluster_stories.title: China's exports ride AI boom as domestic economy struggles
cluster_stories.summary: China's exports saw a significant surge in June, driven by global AI demand and auto sales. Imports also jumped considerably, reaching a five-year high according to customs data. This strong export performance is helping China maintain its trade surplus despite domestic demand challenges. Auto exports alone surpassed one million units for the first time in June. The country's economy relies heavily on overseas markets as domestic consumption struggles.
cluster_stories.headline: China's AI Boom Drives Export Surge to Five-Year High

cluster_stories.title: Chipmaker CXMT seeks $10bn in largest China IPO since 2010
cluster_stories.summary: Chinese group capitalises on boom in demand for AI memory chips
cluster_stories.headline: Chinese AI Chip Maker CXMT Seeks $10B in Largest IPO Since 2010

cluster_stories.title: Samsung, SK hynix, Micron ramp up capacity as demand for AI infrastructure outpaces supply
cluster_stories.summary: Global memory chipmakers are expanding production capacity to meet AI demand. Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are investing billions in new facilities. These companies aim to secure supply for high-bandwidth and DRAM chips. Industry experts anticipate continued tight supplies for several years ahead. Capacity growth will determine memory makers' future market performance.
cluster_stories.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix Race to Expand AI Chip Capacity
